In the second quarter, revenue increased 10% YoY to $19.6B, while card member spending increased 9%, its strongest growth in three years on an FX-adjusted basis. Management raised its FY2026 revenue growth
to 10% and reaffirmed its EPS guidance of $17.30–$17.90.

However, expenses remain a key factor heading into the American Express upcoming quarter. Operating expenses increased 12% YoY to $14.5B in the second quarter as the company spent more on customer engagement, card benefits, and growth initiatives.
partnership that added more than 1M listings to Amex Travel. It also introduced new wellness benefits for U.K. Platinum Card members, expanding its card perks ahead of the earnings report.
Analysts remain broadly positive. Seeking Alpha analysts and Wall Street both rate the stock Buy, with scores of 3.83, while Seeking Alpha's Quant rating is Hold, at 3.20.
with an Outperform rating and a $380 price target, citing growth in the company's premium-card ecosystem.

Seeking Alpha analyst The Value Portfolio also rated the stock Buy, citing double-digit revenue and EPS growth, strong demand across business segments, and premium card-fee revenue that grew 17% YoY for seven consecutive years, reaching nearly $3B quarterly.
Despite these positives, American Express has fallen 12.14% YTD, compared with the S&P 500's (SP500) 13.32% gain. Shares recently traded near $325.31, up about 4% over the week.
American Express has beaten both EPS and revenue estimates in six of its past eight quarters.
Now, investors will watch whether third-quarter results support its full-year guidance and show that revenue growth can keep pace with expenses.
